verdict.rationale: GitBook advertises 'LLM-ready docs' and 'LLM optimizations', and several cited first-party pages were sourced from .md-suffixed URLs (e.g. gitbook-mcp.md, gitbook-cli.md, openapi.md), which implies published pages resolve as markdown. However, no evidence explicitly documents per-page markdown serving or how clean that markdown is, and a probe of the root path gitbook.com/docs.md returned 404. That single root-path miss does not contradict the page-level .md URLs, so this is not a dispute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the .md-suffix behavior for every published page, confirmation that output is clean markdown rather than HTML, coverage of root and index pages (the docs.md probe 404), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, every published page serves clean markdown at its URL (e.g. appending .md) so agents skip the HTML

citations.quote: Tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients can use it to create and configure sites, open change requests, draft content, edit pages, and restructure docs.
